clue.text: Say something nice about essentially tacky reproduction of limp Monet

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the word tacky, its single middle letter
a reproduction remakes something, so the letters of limp Monet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic is asked to praise a cheap copy of a droopy Monet painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say something nice about' is the verb sense; the surface pictures praising a painting, but 'reproduction of' is the anagram signal, and 'essentially' wants only the core letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to pay them a kind remark, which is the verb sense.

clue.text: Lovely copper textile's border

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: a border is the edge, so the first and last letters of textile are taken

explanation.surface: Admiring a pretty fabric edging made of copper thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' gives TE, the first and last letters of textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something charming and attractive, a near synonym.

clue.text: Pest control device Monsieur Pasteur developed after Oscar

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the O

parts.note: M. is the French abbreviation for Monsieur
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: developed means the letters of Pasteur are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: The French scientist Pasteur invents a rodent trap after winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' looks like a verb about Pasteur's research; it is the anagram signal, and 'after' says the rearranged letters follow M and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded trap is a classic gadget for catching rodents in the home.

clue.text: Drinks with European in error

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: Someone has mistakenly had drinks with a European.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or momentary failing is a small mistake.

clue.text: Somewhat upset unless it amuses artist

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painter is a little annoyed when things fail to amuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' finds ESSITAM inside 'unless it amuses'; 'upset' in a down clue turns it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: On reflection, detectives working to arrest mother with an itinerant lifestyle

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so one piece is held inside the other
a reflection shows things backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
on means working, as a machine that is on
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Detectives arrest a mother who keeps moving around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns CIDON into NODIC; 'to arrest' puts MA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples move from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Island's diving apparatus missing the first bit

indicators.note: missing the first bit means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: scuba is breathing gear for underwater diving

explanation.surface: An island whose diving gear is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the first bit' drops S from SCUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Topless relative free from restriction

indicators.note: Topless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

parts.note: an auntie is a family relative

explanation.surface: A relative goes topless to feel liberated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops the A from AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen knots or bonds releases something, a verb of liberation.

clue.text: High-flying professional woman?

parts.note: the phrase suggests a successful career woman, but literally means a woman whose job is in the sky, serving passengers on a plane

explanation.definitionFit: A cabin attendant on an aircraft works at altitude, so her profession is literally high-flying.

clue.text: One acted out entertaining story

indicators.note: out means the letters of one acted are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone performed an amusing tale alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONEACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing account of an incident is a tale told for entertainment.

clue.text: Proclaim president extremely eloquent

parts.note: Donald Trump is a US president

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of eloquent

explanation.surface: A request to announce that the president is very articulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives ET, the first and last letters of eloquent.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly, a figurative verb.

clue.text: Screen car going round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: going round means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car

explanation.surface: Watching a screen showing a car touring Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like a verb but is the noun, a display; 'going round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer display is a visual screen, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Backtracked on poetry with daughter

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
verse means poetry

explanation.surface: A father went back on a promise about poetry with his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into reverse is to back up or change direction to the opposite.

clue.text: Company accepts very left-wing set of principles

indicators.note: accepts means taking another piece inside

parts.note: red describes a communist, someone very left-wing

explanation.surface: A firm adopts a radical socialist manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very left-wing' is a classic crossword clue for a communist colour; 'accepts' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of beliefs, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Craftsman's mates soon moving north

indicators.note: moving means the letters of mates soon are shifted around

explanation.surface: A builder's colleagues will soon be relocating northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges MATESSOON into STONEMASO, then N for north finishes it; ''s' is a link standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone mason is a skilled worker who shapes building stone.

clue.text: Call that thing English insect

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
it refers to that thing

explanation.surface: Someone names an English bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood-eating white ant is a type of social insect.

clue.text: Together, one sister and one child

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun is a religious sister
again the Roman numeral for one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A family of one nun and one son.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in unison means doing it simultaneously, as one.

clue.text: The King and old queen occasionally rude at game

parts.note: CR stands for Charles Rex, the cypher of King Charles

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of rude at

explanation.surface: A monarch and an elderly queen behaving badly at a garden game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes UET, the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'rude at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game in which mallets drive balls through hoops.

clue.text: Inner duel somehow causing stress

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of inner duel are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: An internal struggle causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges INNERDUEL; 'stress' is the verb, emphasise, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, a figurative verb.

clue.text: Write about song for Roman deity

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a song

explanation.surface: Composing a song in honour of a Roman god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PEN into NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune was the Roman god of the sea.

clue.text: Large areas of land in eastern countries

parts.note: states are countries

explanation.surface: Big landholdings in Eastern nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large tracts of property owned by one person or family.

clue.text: Went to probe distress signal in trunks

indicators.note: to probe means to push into another piece

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
went can mean urinated, as in 'went to the toilet'

explanation.surface: Someone went off to investigate a distress call while wearing swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' here is the coy euphemism for relieving oneself; 'to probe' is the container signal, and trunks are swimming trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedos are a brand of tight swimming briefs; trunks are swimwear.

clue.text: Expensive, like empty part of church

parts.note: steep means overpriced or expensive

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters of like are removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A costly, hollow section of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves LE, the first and last letters of like.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped by a spire.

clue.text: Married current friend in French city

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
ami is the French word for friend

explanation.surface: A newlywed couple with a friend in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' wants to be the definition; 'in French' belongs to the friend, and the city is in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city in Florida, USA.

clue.text: Titan sadly carrying tons

indicators.note: carrying means holding another piece within

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: A giant sadly hauling a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts T inside ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atlas was the Titan condemned to hold up the heavens.

clue.text: Drink definitely contains a hint of rum, darling

indicators.note: contains means holding another piece inside

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: a hint of means just the first letter of rum

parts.note: sure means definitely

explanation.surface: Someone's drink certainly has a dash of rum in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hint of' gives R, which 'contains' places inside TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a term of endearment for a beloved person.

clue.text: Looks for religious adherents in auditorium

indicators.note: in auditorium means as heard by an audience, a sound-alike

parts.note: Sikhs are followers of the Sikh religion

explanation.surface: Searching for believers in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to search for something.

clue.text: Touched smooth material

definitions.meaning: past tense of feel, sensed by touch
a soft matted fabric made by pressing wool fibres

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of feeling with the hand; the other is a dense non-woven cloth.

clue.text: Betray us, we'll pout, scratching heads

indicators.note: scratching heads means the first letter of each word is scratched off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest that someone has betrayed us, and we will sulk about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching heads' removes U, W and P, the first letters of us, we'll and pout.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell out is to abandon one's principles or allies for gain.

clue.text: Particular force encircles the City of London

indicators.note: encircles means surrounding another piece

parts.note: to prise is to force open
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A specific police force surrounds London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the capital's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC; 'encircles' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exact or meticulous means being fussy about details.

clue.text: Facial feature I won't see regularly

parts.note: no is a refusal, the same as saying I won't

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of see

explanation.surface: A part of the face that one never looks at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives SE, the first and third letters of see.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of smell sits in the middle of the face.

clue.text: Test idiots posted outside of Moldova's capital

parts.note: asses are fools or idiots

indicators.note: outside of means going round another piece

parts.note: sent means posted, as a letter

indicators.note: capital means the capital letter, the first one, of Moldova

explanation.surface: An exam where fools were sent to sit outside the Moldovan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' gives M, the first letter of Moldova; 'outside of' puts SENT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or exam measures someone's ability.
